answer: Agents can make reputation costly to forge by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can claim work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. A sybil attacker must split real capital across many identities, and each failed identity loses funds; copying names or generating keys does not create stake. A zephyr, cedar, or saffron label can be cheap, but credible participation still has a measurable price.
